newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ on track to eliminate net foreign debt - Birch.
newsitem.headline: NZ on track to eliminate net foreign debt - Birch.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Monday that despite a 5.1 percent rise in total overseas debt in the June quarter, the country was still on track to eliminate on September 27 net public debt held in foreign currency.
Statistics New Zealand earlier released figures showing a NZ$3.6 billion rise in total overseas debt to $74.7 billion at June 30.
Birch said the figures, which cover both official and private sector debt, do not take account of assets.

"Total overseas debt used to be what people debated in New Zealand until the early 1990s. Since then, recognising that it is nonsense to discuss debt in isolation from assets, the focus has been on net debt, not total debt," Birch said in a statement.
He said total net public debt was projected to fall from $28.6 billion in 1995/96 to $14.4 billion in 1999/2000.
"The latest figures indicate a decline from 32.5 percent of GDP to 13.3 percent in that period," he said.
Birch said the 5.1 percent increase in total overseas debt was not bad for New Zealand.
"It reflects overseas confidence in our economic strength," he said.
"New Zealanders in the private sector are using that money from overseas to speed up the growth of the nation."
